title: Schema-first streaming SDK validation playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a proposal for a schema-first approach to validating and enforcing structured outputs for the Hosted API streaming surface, with concrete SDK ergonomics for tool-calling and resumable sessions. This is a practical, incremental PRD draft intended to align product, SDK, and infra teams on the minimal contract we can ship and iterate on.

Problem statement:
- Developers building multi-step integrations (streaming + tool calls) struggle with output shape drift when models change or when partial streams are delivered.
- Current client-side validation is ad-hoc: teams duplicate parsing logic, leading to fragile integrations and silent failures.
- Tool-calling surfaces require predictable handshake semantics (types, partials, retries) that are hard to test across SDKs.

Goals (MUST):
1) Define a compact, schema-first framing for incremental/streamed structured output that is lightweight to validate at the client and server.
2) Provide a small set of SDK primitives (JS + Python protos) that make tool-handshake and resume semantics ergonomic for developers.
3) Wire observability hooks and validation telemetry so runtime regressions are visible and actionable.

Non-goals (for initial launch):
- Full JSON Schema v7 compliance or exhaustive type inference.
- Automatic schema migration tooling across model versions (keep manual for now).

Core proposal:
- Introduce an "Output Schema" artifact: a JSON object with a short id, a version, and a compact shape description. Shape description supports: "primitive", "object", "array", and a small set of annotations (required, partial-ok, stream-fragment). Example id: "rw://hosted/output/v1/email-draft".
- Server-side: streaming responses include an output-schema header on the stream start: X-RW-Output-Schema: rw://hosted/output/v1/email-draft@v3. The stream emits frames with a frame-type: {text, schema-frame, tool-call, error, checkpoint}.
- Schema-frames are incremental JSON deltas that conform to the schema and include stable object ids for merge semantics. They are validated on the server before emission; failing frames are flagged and the stream continues with an error frame.

SDK ergonomics (JS / Python):
- Exported primitive: SchemaValidator(schemaId, options) => validator object with: validate(frame), onInvalid(callback), normalize(frame).
- Streaming client: stream = client.streamGenerate(opts)
  - stream.on('schema', (meta) => // receives schema id + shape)
  - stream.on('fragment', (delta) => validator.validate(delta) // returns normalized patch)
  - stream.on('toolCall', (callMeta) => // client library exposes call helpers)
  - stream.resume(sessionToken) // resumes a checkpointed session; SDK handles reassembly of partial objects.
- Tool-call helper: client.tool.call(toolId, {argsSchema}) returns a ToolInvocation object with lifecycle events: queued, dispatched, result, error. Tool invocations are embedded into the same stream so that clients can associate schema-validated partial results with tool outputs.

Observability and telemetry:
- Validation events: counter + sample of invalid frames (schema id, frame hash, model revision, route). Ingest to Console traces as: validation.failure and validation.repairSuggestion (if normalization applied).
- Latency metrics per frame type (schema-frame, tool-call, text) and per-schema SLOs (p50/p95 assembly time).
- Error tagging: streams that exceed invalid-frame threshold (default 2 per session) escalate to a fallback route (compat-mode) and produce an automatic incident record in the console.

Backward compatibility and rollout strategy:
Phase 0 (alpha): server emits schema header for a small set of curated schemas (email-draft, invoice-items, code-action). SDKs accept header but do not enforce validation by default. Send validation telemetry only.
Phase 1 (beta): enable SDK optional validation flag (client.validateSchema = true). Server-run validation becomes stricter for flagged tenants. Provide a migration guide and a compatibility mode where invalid frames are emitted as error frames instead of aborting streams.
Phase 2 (GA): validation on by default for supported schemas, tooling for schema registration and version pinning in console, and rollback controls for model versions that produce schema regressions.

Vignettes (short):
1) Chat assistant that extracts a structured invoice: schema-frame patches create incremental line items. Client validates patches and updates a local UI table. If a tool call is required to check tax rules, tool-call frames are emitted inline and their results are validated against the expected tax-result schema.
2) Mobile note-taking: low-bandwidth case where fragments arrive across multiple reconnects. SDK resume(sessionToken) replays schema_frames and uses object ids to rehydrate the final object.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Schema expressivity vs. performance: how many annotations do we allow before parsing/validation becomes heavy for mobile SDKs? Suggest limiting to 6 annotations initially.
- Server CPU cost for validation at scale. We need rough cost estimates from infra (ask infra team for RWI-ops estimate).
- How to handle streaming schema evolution when models emit unknown fields? Proposal: treat unknown fields as ignored unless schema marks strict: true.

Next steps (first 6 weeks):
- Build minimal server-side schema header + frame-type plumbing (ENG infra spike; owner: Ethan, ticket RWI-1342). Due: 2024-12-15.
- Prototype JS validator and client hooks (owner: SDK team, PR target: rw-sdk PR#452). Due: 2024-12-22.
- End-to-end playtest with solutions-eng on 2 customers (owners: Sofia, Liam). Set up telemetry dashboards and draft migration notes. Due: 2025-01-19.

Appendix: short schema example
{
  "id": "rw://hosted/output/v1/email-draft@v1",
  "shape": {
    "subject": {"type": "string", "required": true},
    "body": {"type": "string", "stream-fragment": true},
    "recipients": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
  }
}

Notes to reviewers:
- I'm prioritizing a small, pragmatic schema subset to avoid long bikeshedding. Please call out obvious missing primitives (eg datetime, attachments) and we can add in Phase 1.
- Feedback request: which three schemas should be included in Phase 0 pilot? My initial suggestion: email-draft, invoice-items, and code-rewrite-plan.

-- Maya
